key_insight: DFT-trained machine-learning surrogates enable efficient sampling of small-polaron hopping to predict charge conductivity in energy materials.
engineering_relevance: The workflow reduces the computational cost of predicting charge transport in defect-containing Li₄Ti₅O₁₂ battery anodes.
method: Calculate small-polaron hopping barriers using density functional theory.
Train ML surrogates to estimate barriers across polaron configurations.
Feed surrogate predictions into a kinetic model to estimate conductivity.
evidence_signal: Using 154 of 3,649 symmetry-inequivalent barrier calculations, the workflow achieved over 20-fold computational efficiency and predicted room-temperature conductivity of 6.7 × 10⁻³ S/cm, within the experimental range.
watch_item: Transferability to other materials or defect conditions requires validation beyond the demonstrated Li₄Ti₅O₁₂ case.
paper_title: A Machine-learning-aided Workflow for Sampling Small Polaron Dynamics in Energy Materials
